reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's Wednesday. Late July. Nothing special about today — no anniversary, no crisis, no milestone. Just a regular midweek day in the middle of summer, and that's exactly why it matters.

When I was drinking, I couldn't do ordinary Wednesdays. I could do Friday night, I could do vacation, I could do the big event. But a random Wednesday in July, with work in the morning and dishes in the sink and nothing to numb — that was the day I couldn't handle. The lie I told myself was that sobriety would make every day feel like this: gray, functional, small. What I didn't understand yet is that ordinary days are where a life actually gets built. The big moments — the ski trips, the first jump out of a plane, the friendships that go a decade deep — those are just what ordinary days accumulate into when you keep showing up for them.

Durant's line about habit is the whole game. You don't become the person who has a life worth showing up for in one dramatic decision. You become that person on a Wednesday, doing the small unglamorous thing — the meeting, the run, the honest conversation, the going to bed sober again. Today isn't a day to get through. It's a day that counts.
reflection.meditation: What small, ordinary action today is actually part of building the life I want? Can I do it without needing it to feel important?

affirmations: I am building my life on ordinary days, not just the big ones.
Today I have the agency to choose my next action, no matter what I feel.
I am becoming someone I can live with, one honest day at a time.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a regular Wednesday I get to be awake for. Grateful for the quiet things — coffee that actually tastes like coffee, a clear head at 3pm, the ability to make plans and keep them. I remember what it cost to get here, and I don't take a single unremarkable day for granted.
gratitude.closing: One more day. That's the whole thing.
